drivingQuestion: What was the Boethusians' corruption that the mishna refers to?
outcomeNote: narrative baraita; continues in the next unit

segments.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ מִכׇּל אָדָם וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה קִלְקוּל קִלְקְלוּ הַבַּיְיתּוֹסִין? פַּעַם אַחַת בִּקְּשׁוּ בַּיְיתּוֹסִין לְהַטְעוֹת אֶת חֲכָמִים, שָׂכְרוּ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם בְּאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז, אֶחָד מִשֶּׁלָּנוּ, וְאֶחָד מִשֶּׁלָּהֶם.
segments.en: The mishna taught: «Initially, they would accept testimony» to determine the start of the «month from any person,» and this continued until the Boethusians began to corrupt the process. «The Sages taught» a baraita that describes the decisive incident: «What» was the manner of «the corruption» in which «the Boethusians engaged? Once, the Boethusians tried to mislead the Sages» with regard to the day of the new moon. «They hired two people for four hundred dinars» to testify falsely that they had seen the new moon on the thirtieth day of the month. «One» of them was «from our own,» i.e., a member of the Pharisees and the Sages of Israel, «and» the other was «one of theirs.»
